role_in_parent: Reduces the continuum problem on [0,1) to the discrete grid points j/n.
statement_nl: For any integer j with 0 <= j <= n - 1 and any real number x with j/n <= x < (j+1)/n, one has F_n(x) <= F_n(j/n).

domain_restrictions: n is a positive integer (implicit, needed so that j/n and (j+1)/n are well-defined and intervals make sense)
j is an integer satisfying 0 <= j <= n - 1
x is a real number satisfying j/n <= x < (j+1)/n
F_n is defined at every real x considered, and in particular at x equal to j/n
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every positive integer n, for every integer j with 0 <= j <= n - 1, and for every real number x with j/n <= x and x < (j+1)/n, the inequality F_n(x) <= F_n(j/n) holds.

variables.name: n
variables.role: index parameter for the function F_n and for defining interval endpoints j/n and (j+1)/n

variables.name: j
variables.role: cell index that selects the interval [j/n, (j+1)/n)

variables.name: x
variables.role: argument of the function F_n within the interval associated to j

witness_dependencies: none (the claim is universally quantified; no existential witnesses are introduced)
